errors.english: if the two parties—the proponent and the opponent—fail to establish or feel doubt regarding the subject to be understood or the means of understanding, it is problematic
errors.why: go bar bya ba / go bar byed pa are the two persons (the one to be convinced and the one who convinces, glossed next as respondent and proponent), and the root says: even when [a characteristic] is stated, if it is unestablished or doubtful for these two, it is likewise a fallacious proof.

fix.find: if the two parties—the proponent and the opponent—fail to establish or feel doubt regarding the subject to be understood or the means of understanding, it is problematic
fix.replace: even when it is stated, if it is unestablished or doubtful for the two, the one to be convinced and the one who convinces, it is likewise a fallacious proof

note: Accurate commentary on the asiddha examples; only the root lemma on the two parties is misconstrued as 'subject and means of understanding'.

errors.why: The word is (yang) dag par continuing from the previous side: 'is correctly/rightly shown', glossed as 'stated clearly'; nothing about purification.

errors.english: Even if some particular of wind and the others, whichever it may be, is the cause, not every particular would be accompanied by all of desire and the rest
errors.why: The whole sentence from gal te up to 'because it has a definite particular as cooperating condition' is the anticipated objection (zhes dogs pa bsu ba), not the commentator's own statement.

note: Careful construal of a difficult PV commentary passage; one mistranslated word at the opening and the objection's boundary drawn too late.

errors.english: Not making it a particular in that way is for the sake of making it a particular because it does not prove it as it is.
errors.why: The Tibetan says: since what is not qualified in that way does not prove correctly, it must be qualified.

fix.find: Not making it a particular in that way is for the sake of making it a particular because it does not prove it as it is.
fix.replace: Because what is not qualified in that way does not prove [the probandum] as it is, it must be qualified.

errors.english: If you say that the very mention of "proving the probandum" is not what makes it a particular, it is not a particular.
errors.why: The objector's point (rejected in the reply 'that is not a qualification') is that the very mention of 'proving the probandum' IS the qualification; the English makes objection and reply say the same thing.

errors.english: This occurs for the meaning understood as the object
errors.why: don du rtogs pa is 'understood by implication' (arthāt): the qualification applies to the implied sense, since it cannot apply to the word; 'understood as the object' loses the argument.

note: Verse and prose of Dignāga's critique are kept apart and the exception argument is right, but several steps of the qualification debate are garbled.
Faithful rendering of the general/specific and figurative/direct characteristics of the four truths and the two kinds of aspirants.

errors.english: The (sangha) monastic community does not divide the robes.
errors.why: Completing the list from the previous side (washing, dyeing, bowl work, splitting wood): one does not wear the Saṅgha's robes at those times; the Saṅgha is the owner (genitive), not the agent.

fix.find: The (sangha) monastic community does not divide the robes.
fix.replace: One does not wear the robes of the (sangha) monastic community.

errors.english: the son will not return to being the master of the father's house
errors.why: phyir mi ldog pa = does not cease to be: the son remains an owner of the father's household, which is why gifts from him may be accepted.

fix.find: the son will not return to being the master of the father's house
fix.replace: the son does not cease to be an owner of the father's house

errors.english: From the questions asked by the daughter of a brahmin monk
errors.why: The case is that of a monk and a brahmin's daughter (the daughter questioned/asked), not the daughter of a 'brahmin monk'.

note: Usable for a Vinaya-sūtra commentary, but the opening rule and the expelled-son rationale are inverted.

errors.english: "Holder of a Portion," evidently a powerful official, he said
errors.why: The Tibetan only says the goods were marked with the name Dum bu 'dzin pa; 'evidently a powerful official' is the translator's unmarked surmise.

fix.find: "Holder of a Portion," evidently a powerful official, he said

errors.english: yet that is a quality of the sapphire alone
errors.why: The verse argues that quality is not a matter of birth: a glass bead may take on the sapphire's colour and that is its own quality; 'of the sapphire alone' reverses the point.

errors.english: For people born of great families are seen to be no better than dogs
errors.why: The concessive kyang is lost: (some) people, even though born of great families, are seen to be like dogs; the English turns it into a statement about all the high-born.

errors.english: Moon, the captivating one, must be parted from
errors.why: yid 'phrog dang rnam par bral is 'parted from Yid 'phrog / the captivating one': it names what Moon is to be separated from, not an epithet of Moon.

note: Readable and mostly right narrative, but the gnomic verses are bent against their own point and an unmarked guess about the official is inserted.

errors.english: by what means will you honor the Bodhisattva Mahasattva Dharmodgata? Whether it be gold, jewels, pearls, or lapis lazuli...
errors.why: This is a relative clause in the merchant's daughter's offer ('the gold, jewels... with which you will honour Dharmodgata'), not a question to Sadāprarudita.

note: Faithful rendering of the abridged Sadāprarudita citations; one offer turned into a question.

errors.english: through the force of strong attachment
errors.why: lhag par zhen pa is adhyavasāya, the conceptual determination by which a conceptual cognition is said to have distinct particulars as its object, not emotional attachment.

fix.find: through the force of strong attachment

note: Sound rendering of Śākyabuddhi on conceptual cognition and conventional users; one key apoha term wrong.
Accurate translation of the argument on conventions, mantra efficacy and the refutation of manifestation.

errors.why: skad cig ma yin pa'i phyir = 'because it is momentary (a moment)', as the gloss concludes ('its own nature is fixed as momentary').

note: Otherwise a precise rendering of the momentariness argument, including the variant-reading remark; the siddhāntin's reason is negated.
